what_its_for: This medication is used to treat Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in patients 6 years of age and older. It helps improve attention, reduce hyperactivity, and control impulsive behavior by affecting certain chemicals in the brain.
how_to_take: Take this medication by mouth, with or without food, once every morning. Swallow the capsule whole. If you have trouble swallowing capsules, you can open the capsule and sprinkle the entire contents onto a small amount (1 teaspoon) of applesauce. Swallow the mixture right away without chewing. Do not save the mixture for later. Do not crush or chew the capsule or its contents. Take it at the same time each morning to keep a steady routine. Avoid taking it in the afternoon or evening, as it may make it hard to fall asleep at night.
dosing: Your doctor will prescribe the dose that is right for you or your child. The usual starting dose for patients 6 years and older is 39.2 mg/7.8 mg (one capsule) once daily in the morning. Your doctor may increase the dose over time based on how well it works and how it is tolerated. The maximum recommended dose is 52.3 mg/10.4 mg once daily. Always follow your doctor's specific dosing instructions and do not change the dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose the following morning at your regular time. Do not take a double dose to make up for the one you missed. Taking a late dose in the afternoon or evening can cause trouble sleeping.
storage: Store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the medication in a dry place away from light and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep this medication in a secure location out of reach of children and pets. This medication is a controlled substance (Schedule II), so it is important to store it safely to prevent misuse or theft. Dispose of unused or expired capsules properly through a medication take-back program or follow FDA guidelines for safe disposal.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking this medication in the afternoon or evening to prevent difficulty sleeping. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medication, as it may increase side effects. Avoid taking other stimulant medications unless directed by your doctor. Do not take monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) within 14 days of taking this medication, as a dangerous drug interaction can occur. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medication affects you. Limit or avoid caffeine (coffee, tea, energy drinks) as it may worsen side effects like increased heart rate or anxiety.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you or your child experience any of the following: chest pain, shortness of breath, or fainting; fast, pounding, or irregular heartbeat; increased blood pressure; signs of psychosis such as hearing voices, seeing things that are not there, or believing things that are not true; new or worsening aggressive behavior or hostility; signs of circulation problems such as fingers or toes feeling numb, cool, or painful; prolonged or painful erections in males (priapism); significant weight loss or failure to grow as expected in children; severe headache, blurred vision, or signs of stroke; signs of allergic reaction such as rash, hives, or swelling of the face, lips, or throat; thoughts of self-harm or suicide. Also call your doctor if ADHD symptoms do not improve or worsen over time.
when_it_works: This medication is designed to work quickly. Because it contains two active forms of methylphenidate, it starts working within about 1 hour after taking it in the morning and the effects can last up to 13 hours throughout the day. You or your child's teacher or caregivers may notice improvements in attention, focus, and behavior within the first few days of starting treatment. However, it may take a few weeks of regular use and possible dose adjustments for the full benefits to be seen.
special_populations: Children (6 to 17 years): This medication is approved for use in children 6 years and older. Children should be monitored regularly for growth, weight, heart rate, and blood pressure. Older adults (65 years and older): This medication has not been specifically studied in older adults. Use with caution and close medical supervision. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. This medication may harm an unborn baby or pass into breast milk. The risks and benefits should be carefully discussed with your doctor. Patients with heart problems: This medication can increase heart rate and blood pressure. It should not be used in patients with serious heart defects or certain heart conditions. Tell your doctor about any heart problems before starting this medication. Patients with a history of substance abuse: This medication has a potential for abuse and dependence. Use with extreme caution in patients with a personal or family history of drug or alcohol abuse.
